content:
Don Vincente is open again — sort of. The Laredo restaurant reopened recently with its main parking lot closed, only two parking spots available, and service limited to the San Bernardo side of the building. A barricade sits a few feet away, separating it from another restaurant that is still closed.

The restaurant did not close because of anything wrong with the restaurant. According to KGNS, it was shut down by the Oct. 7 DoubleTree Hotel fire — the blaze and its aftermath closed surrounding streets and kept customers away for nearly two weeks. Don Vincente sits just outside what officials call the "collapse zone," so it was cleared to reopen — under restrictions.

The bigger picture

Out-of-town structural engineers arrived Monday, Oct. 19, to survey the DoubleTree, and officials say stabilization could take five to six weeks. That is five to six more weeks of barricades, detours, and closed parking for the businesses on the edge of the zone — businesses that did nothing wrong and are losing money every day they cannot fully open.

Co-owner Nelly Gueta told KGNS the street closures have hit the business hard: "The closing of the streets have really impacted us, they haven't offered any solutions other than opening with restrictions." She hopes the city will offer financial support to the affected small businesses.

What Webb Watch is asking

Will the city offer direct financial relief to the small businesses caught in the collapse zone's shadow — and if so, when and how much? Which restaurants and shops are still fully closed, and what is the city's plan to get customers back to them? The fire was twelve days ago; a real recovery plan for the businesses is still just a hope. We will keep watching.

Sources: KGNS (Elena Stoica), Oct. 19, 2026; Webb Watch 956 reporting.

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, Investigative Reporters, Webb Watch 956

excerpt: Don Vincente is back open — with two parking spots, a barricade feet away, and a co-owner asking where the city's help is. The DoubleTree's collapse zone keeps bleeding small businesses.
title: Open, but Barely: Don Vincente Reopens Under DoubleTree Fire Restrictions
